# Slow SQL: hypotheses, execution evidence and verification

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `sql-query-investigation` · **SQL Server & Data Engineering** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S03-SC001](#S03-SC001)

<p>A query joining several tables is slow in a large database. How would you build an evidence-led investigation and demonstrate that a change helps?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Build a falsifiable investigation of slow SQL and demonstrate whether a targeted change helps.</p>

<ul>
<li>Locate executed SQL and separate observations from candidate causes.</li>
<li>Relate plan, row estimates, predicates, statistics and access paths to observed work.</li>
<li>Compare correctness, logical reads and duration before/after under equivalent conditions.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Index design: an access path that earns its cost](sql-index-design.md)

<p>A multi-table query is slow: what evidence decides the next step? The source scenario covers a broad query investigation, while the stored-procedure prompt narrows the entry point to a call. Both require following observed work into a hypothesis, then checking a change instead of starting with a preferred fix.</p>

### S03-Q036 · Failure cases

<p>A SQL Server stored procedure is slow. How would you locate the expensive work and choose the next investigation using execution evidence?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q036](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q036)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q036](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q036)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Diagnose a slow stored procedure using execution evidence rather than guesswork.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Separate the observed symptom from candidate causes inside or around the procedure. Explain the measurement that would decide between those causes.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Investigate procedure latency through falsifiable hypotheses.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State SQL Server version, representative parameters, workload and available diagnostics. Verify tooling behavior in official documentation; no execution plan or timings are supplied.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Obtains the executed statements, plans, waits and reads relevant to the slow call.</li>
<li>Compares equivalent inputs before/after a change and checks that results remain correct.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Recommending an index or recompilation before identifying the expensive statement and evidence.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you investigate a procedure that is slow only for some parameter values?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S03-SC001 · Production decision

<p>A query joining several tables is slow in a large database. How would you build an evidence-led investigation and demonstrate that a change helps?</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-SC001](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#query-optimization)**

Open the source link for the complete original constraints. The scenario remains one source unit; its original Markdown is also preserved in the shared inventory.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Cover the actual generated query, execution plans, indexing and query profiling/monitoring. Examine whether only required columns and rows are retrieved, cardinality/selectivity, SARGability (whether a predicate permits an index-based search) and statistics.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Organize several diagnostic observations into a justified optimization decision.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use SQL Server with its version, configuration and representative inputs stated; verify diagnostic capabilities in official documentation. Include logical reads and duration, comparing measurements before/after a change under equivalent conditions. All ten source angles remain part of this single scenario.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Prioritizes hypotheses from observed work rather than applying every tuning technique.</li>
<li>Connects the chosen change to its evidence, verifies result correctness and checks workload regressions.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Answering only &#x27;add an index&#x27; or presenting a faster run with different inputs as proof.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which observation would make you investigate row estimates before changing an index?</li>
<li>How would you separate database execution time from time spent transferring or consuming the result?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>An API&#x27;s generated SQL joins orders, items and customers; only some parameter ranges produce slow calls. For the deployed SQL Server version, outline a diagnostic artifact containing the actual query, required rows/columns, plans and relevant measurements. Rank hypotheses about estimates, predicates, indexing or waiting; choose one discriminating check and define a valid before/after comparison.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Names relevant diagnostics and one plausible cause of the slow query.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Prioritizes hypotheses using observations, verifies the exact inputs and result contract, and tests a targeted change with workload regressions considered.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>No captured SQL, plan or comparable measurements are supplied; a proposed optimization cannot be called verified.</p>
